thread:
maya: Heads-up — I'm proposing a tenant-priority eviction + variant fallback flow for when a primary model path hits sustained saturation. Short writeup below.

maya: Problem: some high-throughput tenants are saturating the preferred model pool and causing hard tails for everyone else. Current behavior is to queue or reject; both are bad for latency-SLA customers.

peter: +1 we need something more graceful than bulk rejects. Curious about how you want priorities applied across dedicated vs hosted.

maya: Idea: introduce a short-lived "backoff ticket" that a tenant can acquire when their requests cause local queue depth > X. Ticket triggers 2 actions: 1) route new requests to a cheaper-compatible variant (quantized or small) for up to N seconds, 2) degrade to best-effort rate for that tenant while ticket active.

 sophia: How do we pick "cheaper-compatible variant"? Same tokenizer/format? We can't break customer output expectations.

maya: Good call. We only allow model variants that are API-compatible (same tokenizer + same top-level response schema). Console will surface a per-tenant fallback whitelist configured by product. Default: smaller same-arch family (e.g., 70B -> 13B quantized) with a confidence delta threshold.

raj: What about customer tiering? Premium tenants shouldn't be auto-evicted onto cheaper variants unless they opt-in. Could add a perk to opt out of automated fallback for a higher commitment.

maya: Exactly — default behavior depends on tier. Tier mapping: platinum: manual fallback (alert + canary), gold: auto-fallback with notification, silver/free: auto-fallback immediate. We emit audit events for every swap.

ida: How transient are tickets? Concerned about flip-flopping (hot loops) if tenant traffic is bursty.

maya: Ticket TTL: start at 10s, exponentially backoff up to 2 minutes if tenant keeps getting saturated. Also require a cool-down where we don't fallback back to primary for at least 30s after revert to avoid oscillation.

peter: Telemetry: we need per-route histograms for latency pre/post fallback, counters for ticket acquisition, and a scoreboard showing "fallback cost delta" (tokens/second). Console alert rule should trigger if fallback rate > 5% sustained.

 sophia: UX: console needs a small modal in the tenant page: "Recent auto-fallbacks" with sample requests, before/after model, and a button to pin a variant or opt out. Also a global toggle for ops to enable/disable automated evictions in a region.

raj: API: add a header `X-Fallback-Policy: allow|prefer|deny` that tenants can pass. Server should respect it unless overridden by policy. This lets customers prefer the cheaper variant for cost-sensitive flows.

maya: Implementation sketch: routing layer receives request, consults local queue depth + per-pool saturation metrics. If saturation > threshold, attempt to acquire backoff ticket from distributed coordinator (fast consistent store). If granted, rewrite route to fallback variant and annotate trace `fallback=eviction-ticket`.

 ida: Coordinator single-writer concern — could we use a probabilistic token bucket per pool instead to avoid cross-region locks?

maya: We can do local heuristics to limit coordinator calls: only call when local queue > X and recent global saturation sample exists. Token bucket fallback as a cheap local approximation is OK; coordinator used for final decision for cross-tenant fairness.

peter: We should also surface a simulation mode in console that can run historical traces and show "would have fallbacked" events with expected cost savings and SLA impact. Helps SRE/product decide thresholds.

 sophia: Security/compliance: ensure audit logs include request ids and that fallback doesn't send PII to lower-trust variants (for Private deployments). Maybe a config to disallow fallback entirely for regulated tenants.

maya: Yep — per-tenant policy gates. For private deployments, default to "deny" unless admin enables.

raj: One more thought: when we swap to fallback, we should include a 1-token synthetic prefix in response metadata so clients can detect degraded variant programmatically. e.g., `X-Model-Fallback: true` and `X-Model-Variant: model-13b-q`.

ida: Bootstrapping: propose we run this behind a feature flag in two phases: 1) telemetry-only (no route changes), 2) active-enforcement in a lab org, 3) gradual ramp by tenant tier.

deploy-bot: maya requested prod feature-flag rollout: tenant-eviction-fallback v1 -> staged -> canary region -> global.

maya: Timeline: I'll draft a short RFC with thresholds and telemetry schema. Want a small implementation pod (peter + ida + sophia) to do a 2-week spike. Anyone object?

peter: happy to pair.

 sophia: +1. I'll start on console mockups.

raj: I'll draft billing/contract language for opt-outs.

maya: Cool — I'll drop the RFC link once ready. Thanks all :raised_hands:
